concepts.def: The study of structures that are 1 to 100 nm in size, which is of the order of a few hundred atoms. Nanoscience deals with structures far larger than a single atom but far smaller than anything visible under a light microscope.
A particle 1 to 100 nm across, that is 1 x 10⁻⁹ m to 1 x 10⁻⁷ m. Nanoparticles are smaller than fine particles, so they are the smallest of the three particle sizes named in this section.
Particles with diameters between 100 and 2500 nm, that is between 1 x 10⁻⁷ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m. They are larger than nanoparticles and smaller than coarse particles.
Particles with diameters between 1 x 10⁻⁵ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m, so from 2500 nm up to 10 000 nm. Coarse particles are often referred to as dust, and are the largest of the three sizes.

One thousand-millionth of a metre: 1 nm = 1 x 10⁻⁹ m. A nanometre is one millionth of a millimetre, and a micrometre (1 x 10⁻⁶ m) is a thousand nanometres, so the three particle sizes span from 10⁻⁹ m up to 10⁻⁵ m.

The total surface area of an object divided by its volume. For a cube of side x the surface area is 6x² and the volume is x³, so the ratio is 6x² divided by x³, which is 6 divided by x. The ratio therefore depends only on the size of the cube, not on how much material there is in total.

concepts.term: Effect of size on the ratio
concepts.def: As the side of a cube decreases by a factor of 10 the surface area to volume ratio increases by a factor of 10. Cutting a solid into smaller pieces leaves the total volume unchanged while the total surface area rises, which is why very small particles have very high ratios.

Nanoparticles may have properties different from those for the same materials in bulk because of their high surface area to volume ratio. The material is chemically the same; it is the very large proportion of its atoms that sit on a surface, rather than any change of substance, that makes it behave differently.
Because of the high surface area to volume ratio, smaller quantities of a nanoparticulate material may be needed to be effective than for materials with normal particle sizes.

concepts.term: Nano dimensions against atoms and molecules
concepts.def: An atom has a radius of about 0.1 nm (1 x 10⁻¹⁰ m), so an atom is about 0.2 nm across and a small molecule is a fraction of a nanometre. A 1 nm nanoparticle is therefore only a handful of atoms wide, and a 100 nm nanoparticle roughly 500 atoms wide - which is why 1 to 100 nm structures contain of the order of a few hundred atoms.

Nanoparticles have many applications in medicine, in electronics, in cosmetics and sun creams, as deodorants, and as catalysts. New applications for nanoparticulate materials are an important area of research.

Using the information you are given, weigh the advantages of the nanoparticulate form (often that it works better, or that far less material is needed) against the disadvantages and risks, and then give a judgement that follows from that comparison. An evaluation that reports only one side is not an evaluation.

There are possible risks associated with the use of nanoparticles. Their effects on health and on the environment have not been fully investigated: they are small enough to be breathed in or to pass into cells and the bloodstream, and they are washed into the environment from products such as sun creams and deodorants. Long-term effects are not yet known, so more testing and research are needed.

concepts.term: Why bulk safety data is not enough
concepts.def: A material that is safe to handle in bulk is not automatically safe as nanoparticles, because nanoparticles may have properties different from those of the same material in bulk. The risk has to be assessed for the nanoparticulate form itself rather than assumed from the bulk material.

mcqs.q: A particle is measured and found to have a diameter of 5 x 10⁻⁸ m. Which type of particle is it?
options: A nanoparticle, 1 to 100 nm
A fine particle, PM2.5
A coarse particle, PM10
A single atom, 0.1 nm wide
mcqs.explain: 5 x 10⁻⁸ m is 50 nm, which lies inside the 1 to 100 nm range of nanoscience structures.

mcqs.q: Which list puts the three types of particle in order of increasing diameter?
options: Fine particles, nanoparticles, coarse particles
Coarse particles, fine particles, nanoparticles
Nanoparticles, fine particles, coarse particles
Nanoparticles, coarse particles, fine particles
mcqs.explain: Nanoparticles are 1 to 100 nm, fine particles 100 to 2500 nm and coarse particles 2500 to 10 000 nm.

mcqs.q: According to the specification, coarse particles (PM10) have diameters between which two values?
options: 1 x 10⁻⁷ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m
1 x 10⁻⁹ m and 1 x 10⁻⁷ m
1 x 10⁻⁵ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m
1 x 10⁻⁸ m and 1 x 10⁻⁵ m
mcqs.explain: These are the diameters the specification gives for coarse particles, the ones often referred to as dust.

mcqs.q: An atom has a radius of about 0.1 nm. Approximately how many atoms wide is a nanoparticle of diameter 20 nm?
mcqs.explain: An atom is about 0.2 nm across, so 20 nm divided by 0.2 nm gives about 100 atoms.

mcqs.q: Nanoscience refers to structures 1 to 100 nm in size. This is of the order of how many atoms?
options: Several million atoms
Only one or two atoms
One single large atom
A few hundred atoms
mcqs.explain: The specification states that structures of 1 to 100 nm are of the order of a few hundred atoms.

mcqs.q: A cube of a solid has sides of length 2 cm. What is its surface area to volume ratio?
mcqs.explain: Surface area = 6 x 2² = 24 cm², volume = 2³ = 8 cm³, and 24 divided by 8 is 3.

mcqs.q: The side of a cube is decreased by a factor of 10. What happens to its surface area to volume ratio?
options: It increases by a factor of 100
It increases by a factor of 10
It gets smaller by a factor of 10
It decreases by a factor of 100
mcqs.explain: The specification states this directly, and 6 divided by x confirms it: ten times smaller x, ten times larger ratio.

mcqs.q: A 1 cm cube of a solid is cut into 1000 cubes each of side 1 mm. Which statement about the pieces is correct?
options: The total surface area and the total volume are both 10 times greater
The total volume is 10 times greater and the surface area is unchanged
The total surface area is 100 times greater and the volume is unchanged
The total surface area is 10 times greater and the volume is unchanged
mcqs.explain: The 1000 small cubes have a total volume of 1 cm³, as before, but 60 cm² of surface against the original 6 cm².

mcqs.q: A metal works as a catalyst. Why is it more effective as nanoparticles than as a fine powder of the same mass?
options: The nanoparticles have a much higher surface area to volume ratio
Each nanoparticle has a larger surface area than one fine particle does
The nanoparticles are a chemically different substance from the metal
The nanoparticles have a much lower surface area to volume ratio than the powder
mcqs.explain: Catalysis happens at the surface, and for the same mass the nanoparticles expose far more of it.

mcqs.q: Compared with a material with normal particle sizes, what quantity of the same material as nanoparticles is likely to be needed to be effective?
options: More, because each particle has a very small surface area
More, because so many particles are needed to fill a space
The same, because the material itself is chemically unchanged
Less, because of the high surface area to volume ratio
mcqs.explain: The specification states that smaller quantities may be needed than for materials with normal particle sizes.

mcqs.q: A medicine is made using nanoparticles instead of particles of a normal size. What is the most likely advantage?
options: A smaller quantity of the medicine is needed to be effective
A larger mass is needed because each single particle is smaller
The medicine is changed into a more reactive compound
The surface area to volume ratio of the medicine falls
mcqs.explain: Medicine is one of the applications listed, and the high surface area to volume ratio means less material is needed.

mcqs.q: A deodorant is made with nanoparticles rather than with fine particles of the same material. What is the main reason for this?
options: A smaller quantity is effective, because of the high surface area to volume ratio
Each single nanoparticle has a much greater surface area than any fine particle does
The nanoparticles must be a new substance with different chemical bonds
The surface area to volume ratio falls as the particles are made smaller
mcqs.explain: Deodorants are one of the listed applications, and the specification gives the high ratio as the reason less is needed.

mcqs.q: A sun cream is made in two versions using the same metal oxide. With fine particles it blocks UV well but leaves a white layer, and 5 g is used per application. With nanoparticles it blocks UV equally well, is clear on the skin and 1 g is used, but how much passes through skin has not been fully tested. Which conclusion does this information best support?
options: It is better in every way, so the older cream should not be sold
It works with less material and is clear, but its safety is not yet proven
It must be safe, because it is already being sold as a sun cream
It should not be used at all, because any risk is unacceptable
mcqs.explain: Both sides of the given information are used, and the conclusion is limited to what the data actually shows.

mcqs.q: A factory can buy a catalyst as a fine powder, needing 50 kg at a cost of 2000 pounds, or as nanoparticles, needing 2 kg at a cost of 1600 pounds. The nanoparticle powder can become airborne, and its effects on the lungs have not been fully investigated. Which conclusion does this information best support?
options: The nanoparticles are certainly the safer option, as no harm is reported yet
Less catalyst is needed and it costs less, but workers must be protected
The powder is better, because nanoparticles always harm the workers
The nanoparticles cost less only because they are a different metal
mcqs.explain: The two advantages given are set against the one disadvantage given, and the judgement follows from both.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the possible risks of using nanoparticles is correct?
options: There are no risks, because the same material is safe in its bulk form
There are no risks, because the products containing them are on sale
Their long-term effects on health and the environment are not fully known
The only risk is that nanoparticle materials are expensive to produce
mcqs.explain: The specification requires students to explain that there are possible risks; the incomplete evidence is the reason.

mcqs.q: A metal oxide is safe to handle as a bulk powder. Why does this not show that its nanoparticles are safe?
options: The nanoparticles are made of different atoms from the bulk powder
Each nanoparticle has a larger surface area than a grain of powder
Nanoparticles are far too small to have any effect inside the body
Their very high surface area to volume ratio can change how they behave
mcqs.explain: Nanoparticles may have properties different from those of the same material in bulk, so bulk data does not carry over.
